findings.documented: API key is sent as a query parameter, e.g. GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-...
findings.actual: the key must be sent as the X-API-Key request header; the query param is rejected with 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'
findings.how_found: called an endpoint with ?api_key=... and got a 400 telling me to use the header
findings.impact: every request fails if you follow the documented auth scheme

findings.documented: response is { token, token_type, expires_in: 86400, user:{email,name} }; tokens last 24h; there is no refresh flow
findings.actual: response is { access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in: 900, refresh_url:"/auth/refresh", user:{email} }; the access token lasts 15 minutes and a refresh flow exists
findings.how_found: logged in and inspected the JSON
findings.impact: a client that reads `token` or assumes a 24h session breaks; you must refresh every 15 min to stay logged in

findings.documented: invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: logout is stateless: it returns {ok, note:"tokens are stateless; discard them client side"} and the same access token still returns 200 afterwards
findings.how_found: called /auth/logout, then reused the same token against /v1/saved and got 200
findings.impact: logging out does not revoke access; a leaked token stays valid until it expires

findings.documented: paginate with `page` (1-indexed) and `limit` (max 200); response is { total, page, page_size, results }
findings.actual: pagination is by `limit`/`offset`; `page` is silently ignored; `limit` is capped at 50; response is { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results }
findings.how_found: page=2 returned the same rows as offset=0; limit=200 came back as limit=50; offset paging works
findings.impact: a page-based client re-reads page 1 forever and never advances

findings.documented: `total` is the exact number of matching records; to fetch everything, read total and request total/limit pages
findings.actual: `total` is understated (4178) while paging by has_more yields 4400 distinct records; the documented method drops ~222 listings
findings.how_found: paged until has_more=false and counted 4400 distinct ids vs the reported total of 4178
findings.impact: trusting `total` silently truncates the dataset (~5% of listings missing)

findings.documented: `order` accepts asc (default) or desc
findings.actual: `order` is ignored; results are always ascending by `sort_by` (asc and desc return identical pages)
findings.how_found: compared sort_by=price&order=asc vs sort_by=price&order=desc — byte-identical
findings.impact: you cannot get descending order from the API; must sort client side

findings.documented: the projects section states GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns that project's listings
findings.actual: `project_id` is not an applied filter; the request returns the full unfiltered list (total 4178)
findings.how_found: requested ?project_id=P20173 and got all 4178 records back
findings.impact: you cannot fetch a project's listings through the listings endpoint

findings.documented: area is in square feet, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: a subset of listings report carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square METRES (e.g. a 3 BHK with carpet_area 105); they form a clean sub-200 cluster while real sqft values start above ~400
findings.how_found: carpet-area distribution is bimodal with an empty 200–400 gap for 2/3 BHK; the metric records keep the same super/carpet ratio, so both fields are metric
findings.impact: price-per-sqft and area filters are ~10.76x wrong for these records

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: price_min/price_max are small numbers in [1, 99.9] (crore, i.e. x1e7 rupees); also price_min > price_max for 348/446 projects, so the min/max labels are unreliable
findings.how_found: scanned all 446 projects; values never exceed 99.9 and min > max most of the time
findings.impact: reading them as rupees is off by seven orders of magnitude; a price range cannot be trusted

findings.documented: each record describes a real listing and "anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user"
findings.actual: 30 listings are physically impossible: 10 with a negative price, 10 with floor > total_floors, 10 with carpet_area > super_built_up_area
findings.how_found: checked these invariants across the full crawl
findings.impact: impossible records reach the UI and corrupt any aggregate that includes them

findings.documented: posted_by_contact is the seller's verified contact number; is_verified means our operations team checked the listing
findings.actual: 261 listings come from 12 phone numbers that each post under several different seller names (invented agencies + rotating personal names) and are systematically under-priced (median ~₹6.6k/sqft vs ~₹9.9k) to farm enquiries; most are flagged is_verified=true
findings.how_found: grouped listings by phone number; exactly 12 numbers map to more than one seller name, and their price-per-sqft sits well below the market
findings.impact: enquiry-bait fraud is shown to users as verified inventory

findings.documented: every listing_id is globally unique and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: about 145 listings are second copies of the same physical unit cross-posted on another website (same building/locality/bedroom/bathroom/floor and near-identical coordinates), so 4400 records describe roughly 4255 properties
findings.how_found: clustered records by physical attributes plus coordinate proximity
findings.impact: property counts and "similar" strips double-count the same flat

findings.documented: returns only active listings; inactive, expired and withdrawn are excluded, so anything returned is safe to show
findings.actual: 923 of 4400 listings have is_live=false and are still returned; the is_live field itself is undocumented
findings.how_found: counted is_live across the crawl
findings.impact: withdrawn/inactive listings are served and shown as if active

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing
findings.actual: that path 404s; the working path is the plural GET /v1/listings/{id}
findings.how_found: requested both the singular and plural paths
findings.impact: a detail page built to the docs 404s on every listing

findings.documented: returns up to ten comparable listings for a "you may also like" strip
findings.actual: no similar endpoint exists at any path (all variants 404)
findings.how_found: requested the documented path and several plausible variants — all 404
findings.impact: there is no comparable-listings data from the API; it must be computed client side

findings.documented: GET/POST/DELETE /v1/favourites, POST body { id }
findings.actual: /v1/favourites 404s; the real endpoint is /v1/saved and POST expects { listing_id }
findings.how_found: requested /v1/favourites (404), then probed and found /v1/saved
findings.impact: the favourites feature is broken end-to-end if built to the docs

findings.documented: not mentioned anywhere in the reference
findings.actual: exists and is the real favourites API: GET /v1/saved -> {count, results}, POST {listing_id} -> {ok, listing_id, saved_count}, DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id}
findings.how_found: probed saved-listing paths after /v1/favourites 404'd
findings.impact: the working favourites API is entirely undocumented

findings.documented: returns pre-computed city aggregates for a dashboard
findings.actual: the path 404s; no analytics endpoint exists at any variant
findings.how_found: requested /v1/analytics/summary and variants (/v1/insights/summary, /v1/stats, ...) — all 404
findings.impact: the insights screen must compute every aggregate itself from the crawl

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed on every change and always agrees with GET /v1/listings?project_id=...
findings.actual: total_listings disagrees with the actual live-listing count for 129 projects; and since project_id is ignored, the documented cross-check cannot even be run
findings.how_found: counted listings per project_id from the crawl and compared to each project's total_listings
findings.impact: project listing counts cannot be trusted

findings.documented: timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z suffix, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: the service reports its own clock in IST (+05:30 in /health and reference_date), while record timestamps carry a UTC Z; the record wall-clock values line up with the IST reference, so the Z is a mislabel and they must be read as IST
findings.how_found: compared the +05:30 clock in /health against the Z-suffixed posted_at values when counting the 7-day IST window
findings.impact: treating posted_at as true UTC shifts every record 5h30m and miscounts date-window queries
